extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemaking stakeholders (regulated facilities, state agencies, Tribes, environmental groups, and public commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register proposed rule by EPA to revise the 2008 Billings/Laurel SO2 Federal Implementation Plan (FIP) by removing affirmative defense provisions for flare emission limit exceedances during malfunctions, startups, and shutdowns. The document explains the technical emission limits and monitoring methods, legal and policy rationales, public comment procedures, and required statutory/EO reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed removal of affirmative defense provisions (§52.1392(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is proposing to revise the 2008 Billings/Laurel SO2 FIP by removing §52.1392(i) and all of the provisions therein, including paragraphs §52.1392(i)(1)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the removal is proposed pursuant to the Clean Air Act (CAA) and the Agency's SSM policy (2015 SSM SIP Action and 2021 Memorandum) and consistent with the D.C. Circuit decision in Environ. Comm. Fl. Elec. Power v. EPA. The EPA finds the affirmative defense provisions to be 'specific relief' that would block aspects of the Act's enforcement regime; therefore they are substantially inadequate to meet CAA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare emission limits in the 2008 FIP
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2008 Billings/Laurel SO2 FIP established flare emission limits: 150 lbs SO2 per 3-hour period at all but the Jupiter Sulfur flare, and a 75 lbs SO2 per 3-hour period shared limit for the Jupiter Sulfur flare and the Jupiter Sulfur SRU/ATS stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric limits apply to the four named sources (CHS Laurel Refinery, Phillips 66 Billings Refinery including Jupiter Sulfur, ExxonMobil/Par Montana Billings Refinery, and Montana Sulphur and Chemical Company). The proposed action does not change these numeric limits, but addresses the affirmative defense provisions tied to exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and compliance determination methods for flare emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine flare emissions, the 2008 FIP required concentration monitoring (which can consist of continuous monitoring, grab sampling, or integrated sampling) and continuous flow monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These monitoring methods are the compliance-determining methods for the FIP flare limits; they remain the basis for assessing exceedances. The rule text and preamble describe these methods as the required approach for determining emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of the affirmative defense (as previously promulgated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2008 rule provided an affirmative defense to penalties for violations of flare limits during malfunctions, startups, and shutdowns; 'The elements of the defense, which a source would have to prove in court or before an administrative judge, are enumerated in our 2008 final rule and are consistent with the elements described in our 1999 excess emissions memorandum.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2008 provision required timely notification (see §52.1392(i)(2)) and proof by a preponderance of evidence to establish the defense. The preamble explains these elements were intended to provide relief for 'truly unavoidable violations' while maintaining incentives for compliance. The current proposal would remove those elements from the FIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal standard on SSM provisions and affirmative defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP or FIP provisions that provide exemptions or affirmative defenses for excess emissions during periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) are inconsistent with CAA requirements according to the EPA's 2015 SSM SIP Action and the 2021 Memorandum; court decisions (e.g., NRDC v. EPA, Environ. Comm. Fl. Elec. Power v. EPA) have shaped and limited EPA authority regarding affirmative defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key legal points: (a) CAA sections 113 and 304 limit the agency's authority to create affirmative defenses that alter federal courts' jurisdiction to assess penalties; (b) the D.C. Circuit found some affirmative defenses constitute 'specific relief' that block enforcement and upheld EPA's SSM policy regarding such affirmative defenses; (c) EPA distinguishes between malfunctions (unforeseen) and planned events (startup/shutdown) with respect to appropriateness of defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission requirements and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments must be received on or before December 16, 2024. Submit comments, identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R08-OAR-2023-0587, to the Federal Rulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow online instructions for submitting comments. Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed. The EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Do not submit electronically any information considered Confidential Business Information (CBI) or otherwise restricted by statute. Multimedia submissions must be accompanied by a written comment (the written comment is the official comment). The EPA generally will not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing systems). For additional submission methods, contact the person in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section. See EPA public comment policy at https://www2.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing request procedure and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Public hearing: If anyone contacts the EPA requesting a public hearing on or before October 30, 2024, the EPA will hold a hearing. Contact Adam Clark at clark.adam@epa.gov to request a hearing or to determine if a hearing will be held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hearing is requested, additional information about the hearing will be published in a subsequent Federal Register document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and confidentiality limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents in the docket are listed in the https://www.regulations.gov index, but although listed some information is not publicly available (e.g., CBI or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute). Certain other material, such as copyrighted material, will be publicly available only in hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For alternative arrangements to access docket materials, email or call the person listed in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section. Agencies may review submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions or portions thereof; submitted comments may not be readable until the agency has approved them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice (EJ) screening and use of EJScreen
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA defines environmental justice as 'the fair treatment and meaningful involvement of all people regardless of race, color, national origin, or income' and performed EJ screening analyses using EJScreen for ~5 km buffers around the four facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EJScreen provides environmental indicators (PM2.5, ozone, traffic proximity/volume, percent pre-1960 housing, proximity to Superfund/RMP/hazardous waste) and demographic indicators (percent low-income, communities of color, linguistic isolation, less than high school education). EJScreen is a screening tool, not for in-depth risk analysis, and is subject to uncertainty. EPA used 5-km buffers and an 80th-percentile initial filter; results are informational and not the basis of the proposed action. Full EJScreen reports are in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and Executive Order review determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's administrative determinations for the proposed action under various statutes and executive orders are provided (Executive Order 12866, Paperwork Reduction Act, Regulatory Flexibility Act, Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, Executive Order 13132 Federalism, Executive Order 13175 Tribal consultations, Executive Order 13045, Executive Order 13211, National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act, Executive Order 12898/14096).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key determinations in the preamble: (a) Exempt from E.O. 12866 review as not a rule of general applicability (applies to 4 facilities); (b) No information collection burden under the PRA; (c) Certifies no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA; (d) No unfunded mandate under UMRA; (e) No federalism implications; (f) No Tribal implications (does not apply on reservation lands); (g) Not subject to EO 13045; (h) Not a significant regulatory action under EO 13211; (i) Does not involve technical standards under NTTAA; (j) EPA believes it is not practicable to assess disproportionate impacts prior to the action but expects neutral to positive air quality impacts; EJScreen results provided for informational purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents and legal authorities to consult
rubrics_metrics.description: The docket and the preamble reference supporting documents, guidance memos, and court decisions relevant to the proposed action (e.g., 2015 SSM SIP Action, 1999 SSM Guidance, 2020 and 2021 memoranda, NRDC v. EPA, Environ. Comm. Fl. Elec. Power v. EPA, Montana Sulphur and Chemical Co. v. U.S. EPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting documents available in the docket include EPA guidance memos, court decisions, and EJScreen reports. The formal authority citation: 42 U.S.C. 7401 et seq. The rule text instructs amendment to 40 CFR part 52 to remove and reserve paragraph (i) of §52.1392.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multimedia and non-textual submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment; the written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points the submitter wishes to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will generally not consider comments or contents located outside the primary submission (e.g., on web/cloud/file-sharing). Ensure all substantive material is included in the written submission uploaded to the docket.
